sources.title: Spider-Man: conheça os 6 principais jogos do Homem-Aranha
sources.text: Muitos personagens dos quadrinhos ganharam destaque nos videogames ao longo dos anos, mas não dá para negar que nosso querido Homem-Aranha é um dos mais emblemáticos. Desde os tempos do Atari, no início dos anos 1980, o herói já ganhou dezenas de adaptações, para todo tipo de plataforma e com resultados muito variados. Por muito tempo, os jogos do Aranha oscilaram entre aqueles mais apressados para casar com o lançamento de filmes e experiências mais ambiciosas, que tentavam capturar o que torna o herói único: a sensação de balançar entre os prédios de Nova York, a agilidade nas lutas e o peso emocional de ser Peter Parker. Nem todos os jogos, porém, ficaram na memória dos fãs. Alguns definiram o que se espera de um game do personagem, seja pela liberdade de exploração, pela fidelidade ao espírito dos quadrinhos ou pela qualidade da narrativa. Por isso, separamos os principais jogos do Homem-Aranha em ordem cronológica . Confira! Há inúmeros jogos inspirados no herói mais querido da Marvel, então optamos por listar os que são considerados os principais. Lançado pela Activision e desenvolvido pela Neversoft, o Spider-Man de 2000 foi o primeiro grande sucesso do herói na era 3D . Chegou ao PlayStation, Nintendo 64 , Dreamcast e PC, e apostou em uma história original que reunia parte da galeria de vilões do herói, como Doutor Octopus, Venom e Carnage, em uma trama inspirada em um desenho animado dos anos 1990. O jogo ganhou destaque também pela presença de Stan Lee, que aparece como ele mesmo na narrativa. O jogo ainda era linear, dividido em fases, mas transmitia bem a acrobacia e o clima de aventura de uma revista em quadrinhos. Para muita gente, foi a primeira vez que um game do Aranha realmente parecia à altura do personagem, e ele abriu caminho para o que viria depois. Baseado no filme de Sam Raimi, com Tobey Maguire no papel principal, Spider-Man 2 é lembrado até hoje como um dos maiores marcos da franquia , e o motivo tem nome: liberdade. Desenvolvido pela Treyarch, o jogo colocou o jogador em uma Nova York aberta, que podia ser explorada livremente, com missões paralelas, criminosos aleatórios para deter e cidadãos para ajudar. O grande diferencial era o sistema de balanço. Em vez de atirar teias em um ponto fixo do céu, o herói realmente se prendia aos edifícios, com controles que davam a sensação de física e de peso. Até hoje, muitos fãs afirmam que essa foi uma das melhores representações do movimento do Aranha até a chegada da nova geração de jogos. Tobey Maguire e Alfred Molina, o Doutor Octopus, emprestaram suas vozes aos personagens , o que reforçou a ligação com o filme. Também desenvolvido pela Treyarch, Web of Shadows adotou um tom mais sombrio e maduro que os títulos anteriores . A história mostra Nova York invadida por criaturas simbióticas, e o jogador precisa lidar com a ameaça enquanto se relaciona com aliados como Mary Jane, Gata Negra e Wolverine, além de enfrentar Venom. O ponto mais marcante era o sistema de escolhas. Ao longo da campanha, o jogador decidia entre o caminho do herói e a influência do simbionte, alternando entre o traje clássico e o traje negro, e essas decisões alteravam parte da narrativa e o final do jogo. O combate ágil, com combos aéreos e golpes em paredes, também ajudou a consolidar o título como um dos favoritos de quem cresceu na era do PlayStation 3 e do Xbox 360. Depois de anos de altos e baixos, o Homem-Aranha finalmente recebeu um tratamento de superprodução com Marvel’s Spider-Man, da Insomniac Games , lançado em 2018 para PlayStation 4. A história acompanha um Peter Parker já experiente, com oito anos de carreira como herói, tentando equilibrar a vida pessoal, o trabalho e a luta contra o crime enquanto uma nova ameaça, liderada por Mister Negative e envolvendo figuras como Kingpin e Doutor Octopus, ameaça a cidade. O jogo brilha por combinar quase tudo o que os fãs esperavam: uma Nova York detalhada, um sistema de balanço fluido e viciante, um combate inspirado nos jogos do Batman da série Arkham e uma narrativa emocional , que trata Peter e Otto Octavius com surpreendente profundidade. Vendeu mais de 20 milhões de cópias, ganhou uma versão remasterizada para PlayStation 5 e chegou ao PC em 2022, o que ampliou ainda mais seu alcance. Lançado como título de estreia do PlayStation 5, Miles Morales continua a história da Insomniac , mas troca o protagonista. Agora, o foco é o jovem Miles, que acaba de herdar os poderes de Peter Parker e precisa proteger o Harlem e sua comunidade durante um inverno rigoroso em Nova York. Sua identidade é marcada por habilidades próprias, como os ataques de bioeletricidade, chamados de “Venom”, e a capacidade de camuflagem. Com uma campanha mais curta que a do jogo de 2018, mas igualmente intensa, o título se destaca pelo carisma do protagonista, pelo tom mais pessoal da história e pelo visual impressionante para a época. A trama envolve a corporação Roxxon e o Tinkerer, e mostra que o legado do Aranha pode ser carregado por mais de uma pessoa. O terceiro capítulo da série da Insomniac chegou ao PlayStation 5 em 2023 e elevou a escala da franquia. Pela primeira vez, o jogador alterna livremente entre Peter Parker e Miles Morales , em uma Nova York ampliada, que agora inclui os distritos do Brooklyn e do Queens. As novas asas de teia e os túneis de balanço rápido tornaram a exploração ainda mais dinâmica. A história traz Kraven, o Caçador, e uma das versões mais fortes de Venom já vistas nos games , com Tony Todd na voz do simbionte, além do impacto do traje negro sobre Peter e de seu conflito com Harry Osborn. O jogo vendeu mais de 10 milhões de cópias e chegou ao PC em janeiro de 2025. É considerado por muitos o ponto mais alto da franquia até agora, tanto pela ambição da narrativa quanto pela evolução das mecânicas. Gostou de conferir os principais jogos do Homem-Aranha? Deixe seu comentário nos dizendo quais são os seus favoritos! De onde veio o sinal de rádio captado pela primeira vez fora do Sistema

sources.title: The latest game from the creator of Dragon Quest was made in ‘about 30 minutes’ with AI
sources.text: Horii has previously praised AI technology and its use in video games Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii has released a new game, which he claims was made in “just about 30 minutes,” with generative AI. Horii,Â age 72, who is best known as the creator of the Dragon Quest franchise and for his work on the beloved RPG Chrono Trigger, took to X to show off his latest game. “Long ago, when I made ‘The Portopia Serial Murder Case’ on a PC , I came up with the story myself, drew the pictures myself, did the programming myself, and created the game all by myself,” Horii said. “And now, by using AI, even if I can’t draw pictures or program, I can just give instructions to the AI and create a decent game all by myself. It’s truly astonishing. By the way, the production time for the game below was just about 30 minutes. Oh, and don’t press the boost button.” In the new game, Interrogation Room Komiya, players select a series of text prompts in an attempt to make a suspect confess to a crime. ãã®æãPCã§ããã¼ããã¢é£ç¶æ®ºäººäºä»¶ããä½ã£ãæã¯ãèªåã§ç©èªãèããçµµãæãã¦ããã­ã°ã©ã ããã¦ãã²ã¨ãã§ã²ã¼ã ãä½ãã¾ãããããã¦ä»ãï¼¡ï¼©ãä½¿ãã°ãçµµãæããªãã¦ãããã­ã°ã©ã ããªãã¦ããï¼¡ï¼©ã«æå³ããã ãã§ãã²ã¨ãã§ãããããã®ã²ã¼ã ãä½ãã¦ãã¾ãã¾ãããã³ãã³ã£ããã§ããâ¦ This isn’t the first time Horii has praised generative AI technology. Last year, Horii claimed that he was thinking about adding an AI chatbot to one of his future games.Â During the G-Star 2025 games conference in South Korea. “It would be interesting if we could use that kind of AI to, for example, play quiz games or mystery games where you have to find the culprit,” he explained, perhaps foreshadowing this latest release. “You could find the culprit while talking to your subordinates. Or the AI ââcould do the interrogation and when you ask it, it could tell you ‘here’s what they said’. Actually solving the case through conversation, while chatting… if something like that were truly possible, it would be fun, wouldn’t it?” As reported by Automaton at the time the interviewer than asked Horii if he was considering incorporating AI into his future games, to which he reportedly replied “yes”. Horii has worked on every mainline Dragon Quest game since the 1986 original, and via his company Armor Project, co-owns the franchise alongside Square Enix . Generative AI remains a contentious subject in video games, particularly because of concerns about plagiarism and the perceived poor quality of its results. However, many developers are using AI in the creation of their games, in an attempt to lower costs and speed up development. While AI creation remains a grey area in much of the world, with governments, artists, and companies deliberating how best to move forward, Japan declared in 2023 that using datasets to train AI models doesnât violate copyright law, even for commercial use. A recent report on Japanese online game developers claims that 100% of those surveyed use generative AI tools. The Japan Online Game Association (JOGA) stressed that this report relates only to domestic (Japanese) games that are âplayed via the internet regardless of deviceâ. It doesnât include console or PC games , nor does it include mobile games that are standalone offline experiences.

sources.title: Dragon Quest creator continues love affair with AI as he releases a game he generated in 30 minutes
sources.text: Just keep the slop out of Dragon Quest 12, please Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii is touting his new game which he claims took him about 30 minutes to make using generative AI. Despite being one of the most prolific game creators of all time, the Dragon Quest creator has fallen head over heels for the slop machine like your elderly uncle on Facebook. Developers like Hideo Kojima have spoken critically about using it as a replacement for creative aspects of game development , but Square Enix is working with Google on a chatbot for Dragon Quest 10, and Horii has generally been very positive about the tech, claiming it can make JRPG characters "feel even more human" and claiming that the tech known for hallucinating info "hardly ever makes things up." And now, Horii has released a new 'game' titled Interrogation Room Komiya (via VGC ). The developer went to Twitter recalling the development of his 1983 adventure game The Portopia Serial Murder Case – a game which he wrote, programmed and created art for all by himself – while now, he can just write some words into the machine, allowing him to make something in about 30 minutes. Of course, the question is whether Horii's enthusiasm for the tech will carry over into Dragon Quest 12, which has been in what could be described as development hell, given that the entire concept was reworked and development was restarted . The game is confirmed to have artwork and characters from Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama and series composer Koichi Sugiyama, both of whom have passed away since the 12th entry was announced. I'm a creature-collecting sicko, and going hands-on with Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World made me realize how much I've been missing out on this spin-off. sources.text: AI Dragon Quest Portopia Serial Murder Case Yuji Horii Yuji Horii, best known for his work on the Dragon Quest RPG franchise , is also known in Japan for creating a murder mystery adventure The Portopia Serial Murder Case . That game was released in 1983 for PC titles and is credited with helping to pave the way for Nintendoâs own Famicom Detective Club series. Unfortunately, outside of Japan, Portopia has mostly been known for Square Enixâs attempts to revitalize the game entirely using AI for a maligned 2023 remake . Not content with leaving the AI experiments solely to other people, Horii himself decided to try “developing” his own spiritual successor using Claude. That game is called Komiya in the Interrogation Room and it’s a short browser-based experience that takes place entirely within the confines of the interrogation of the titular 72-year-old suspect Komiya for a possible safe robbery. Due to the suspect’s constant lies, the player must use various lines of questioning the game provides to uncover the truth underneath them, all while balancing Agitation and Resistance meters. sources.title: Dragon Quest co-creator Yuji Horii releases new AI-generated game, and he says it took 30 minutes to make
sources.text: Dragon Quest co-creator Yuji Horii has just released a new game that he says was made (or, rather, prompted) in about half an hour thanks to gen-AI. In an online post from this weekend, the famed game developer recalled how he created 1983's The Portopia Serial Murder Case mostly on his lonesome. "I came up with the story myself, drew the pictures myself, did the programming myself, and created the game all by myself," Horii wrote on X. "And now, by using AI, even if I can't draw pictures or program, I can just give instructions to the AI and create a decent game all by myself. It's truly astonishing. By the way, the production time for the game below was just about 30 minutes. Oh, and don't press the boost button," he adds, while linking to a text-based interrogation game. その昔、PCで『ポートピア連続殺人事件』を作った時は、自分で物語を考え、絵も描いて、プログラムもして、ひとりでゲームを作りました。そして今、ＡＩを使えば、絵を描けなくても、プログラムしなくても、ＡＩに指図するだけで、ひとりで、そこそこのゲームを作れてしまいます。ホントびっくりです。ちなみに下のゲームの制作時間は、ほんの30分ほどでしたよ。あ、ブーストするボタンは押さないように。 https://t.co/slczyG52ZQ Horii's love affair with the tech started a while ago. Earlier this year, MMO Dragon Quest 10 teamed up with Google's Gemini AI to power an NPC chatbot called "Chatty Slimey", an in-game character that can talk to players in case they're, you know, starving for human interaction in a massively multiplayer online RPG. The 72-year-old dev defended the decision in an interview with Famitsu , translated by GamesRadar , months later: "Because nowadays AI is really smart, it's fun. It doesn't matter what I ask it, it hardly ever makes things up [anymore]... It's evolving, and lately there are a lot of things you can do with it. Slimey is a conversational partner, so I think it lowers the barrier of entry to interacting with AI." As noted by VGC , Horii is also toying with the idea of an AI-powered chatbot for one of his future games, as well. He's currently involved with Dragon Quest 12: Beyond Dreams and a surprise sequel to The Portopia Serial Murder Case decades in the making. Generative-AI and its uses in game development have been hugely controversial in recent years - with players, developers and video game actors worried about job security . Just this month, Google and Unity revealed a quite depressing AI-game-making tool , too.

sources.title: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction Release Date Confirmed
sources.text: He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction has a release date: February 4, 2027. Bitmap Bureau, the developer behind Terminator 2D: No Fate, worked with Mattel and the retro team at Clear River Games on the old-school brawler, which launches digitally and physically on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. Two physical versions of the game will be available via Limited Run Games. The standard physical release costs $29.99, and the Collector’s Edition costs $99.99. Dragon Pearl of Destruction is inspired by the much-loved ‘80s animated series, and you can see that come through in pixel-art and 2D gameplay. The playable characters are He-Man, She-Ra, Man-At-Arms, and Teela, and you can play solo or co-op (two-player local co-op). There are 13 stages, including the Royal Palace, the Vine Jungle, and Snake Mountain, and famous villains such as Skeletor, Evil-Lyn, Beast Man, and Trap Jaw. You’ll also bump into the dark sorceress Shokoti and the Shadow Beasts. The Collector’s Edition includes lunchbox style packaging, pin badges, a mini-power sword, and an acrylic standee featuring He-Man riding Battle Cat, among other things. The contents of both physical editions are detailed below. We previewed He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction in August and thought it could be the first ever good He-Man game. It comes following the release of Amazon’s Masters of the Universe, which struggled at the box office but found success on Prime Video. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

Here is an overview of the game, via Limited Run Games: Inspired by the iconic ’80s cartoon, He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction allows players to take control of Eternia’s beloved heroes, including He-Man, Teela, Man-At-Arms, and more, to battle Skeletor and Evil-Lyn and save Eternia from plunging into darkness. Fight through over 13 action-packed levels using character-specific moves, abilities, and power-ups to stop Skeletor’s ancient ritual that threatens to take over Eternia. Battle Cat, He-Man’s fearless feline companion, also joins the fray, battling on the side of justice with his claws unsheathed.

sources.title: He-Man Sets Official Return in 2027 With 'Dragon Pearl of Destruction'
sources.text: The Masters of the Universe are here in all their pixelated glory Just in time for He-Man’s birthday, Clear River Games revealed the release date for He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction, an upcoming action game based on this long-running series. Thankfully, the wait for Prince Adam and his buddies won't be long. Clear River Games also confirmed that Dragon Pearl of Destruction will have a physical release for Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X. It will also be available digitally on those platforms, as well as PS4, Windows PC, and Xbox One. The game will be released on Feb. 4, 2027. He-Man and the Masters of the Universe: Dragon Pearl of Destruction is a retro-style beat ‘em up. The game is being developed by Bitmap Bureau, a studio that’s quite familiar with arcade-era-inspired tie-ins to classic franchises. In 2025, the team released the 2D run-and-gun Terminator 2D: No Fate , which received solid reviews despite criticisms for its short length. Before that, the team worked on the beat ‘em up Final Vendetta and the hack-and-slash Battle Axe . Dragon Pearl of Destruction has four playable characters — He-Man, Teela, Man-at-Arms, and She-Ra — each with different movesets and magic abilities. The Steam page indicates it will have 13 levels, suggesting a relatively short playtime, as is fairly common in this genre. Beyond the upcoming game, He-Man recently hit the screen in this summer’s Masters of the Universe live-action movie. While the film performed relatively well with critics , it flopped at the box office, grossing $114 million on a $170 to 200 million budget, although it was Prime Video’s most-streamed movie for several weeks in a row. A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later. Beyond this, there have been plenty of recent He-Man TV shows. The animated series Masters of the Universe ran on Netflix from July 2021 to January 2024 for 15 episodes total. Before that, She-Ra: Princesses of Power ran from 2018 to 2020 for 52 episodes, a reboot of the ‘80s series (which was a spin-off of He-Man and the Masters of the Universe ). That series received critical acclaim and attracted a large fandom thanks to its interesting characters, strong writing, and central queer relationship between She-Ra and Catra.

stories.title: Haunted Chocolatier 'More of an Action RPG' Compared to Stardew Valley, ConcernedApe Says
stories.summary: Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Haunted Chocolatier 'More of an Action RPG' Compared to Stardew Valley, ConcernedApe Says
sources.text: Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has briefly discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier . Barone announced Haunted Chocolatier back in 2021, but amid ongoing work on his phenomenally successful Stardew Valley, progress on the follow-up has been slow going. Indeed, in June, Barone admitted to feeling somewhat embarrassed to have to keep on saying he was still working away on the game. “Feels kinda dumb posting this same thing over and over, but that’s the reality,” he said at the time. In a new interview with GQ (thanks, Eurogamer ), Barone touched on what to expect from Haunted Chocolatier when it eventually comes out, and it sounds more different from Stardew Valley than I had expected. It’s set in a more “metaphysical” locale, for a start, and in terms of gameplay it’s more of an action RPG. “It is still what I call a town game,” Barone said, “But it’s more of an action RPG — the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights. It's for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly.” In June, Barone admitted fussing over every last detail in a bid to make Haunted Chocolatier as close to perfect as humanly possible . “I am being very thoughtful about every aspect of the game,” he said at the time. “The things in the game which the player will be interacting with or using very often need to be ‘perfect.’ They need to be seamless, clear, intuitive, satisfying, aesthetic.” He used the example of iterating on the recipe book for making chocolates, which sounded like a significant challenge. “To me, it’s not a simple task, as I torture myself over every last detail,” he said. “This is a UI you will be using fairly often, so it has to be perfect. You need to be able to accomplish your goal with the minimal number of clicks. There needs to be just the right amount of data presented to the player: not so much as to be overwhelming, but not so little as to be trivial or mundane. And the way that this data is laid out on the page is crucial… If the data is all clustered together, it will be disgusting to look at. The data needs to be grouped into compelling, intuitive and easy to read/understand groupings. It needs to look appealing and intriguing. And this is just the bare minimum, that players will likely take for granted. If all of that is accomplished then the player is now comfortable while perusing the recipe book. But I want more than just comfort. I want to delight the player. All of this typically requires me to iterate on something several times before I’m satisfied with it.” Barone also explained why he didn't want to show Haunted Chocolatier off too much at this stage of development. “Partly, it feels like I’m serving a half-baked bread. I would rather serve a fully baked bread,” he said. “Also, I know that many parts of the game will likely evolve and change before release, so if I reveal them early, I risk disappointing players if the final product does not match their expectation. Fortunately, I’m in a position where I don’t need to market the game, so I can take my preferred approach.” Haunted Chocolatier is so far without a release date, as is Stardew Valley 1.7 update, which Barone isn’t working on directly. Earlier this year, he explained his current way of working in an interview with IGN . “Well, part of the reason why I've expanded my team a little bit is so that hopefully I can spend more time working on Haunted Chocolatier," he told us in February. "And it's worked out pretty well so far, I would say. On 1.7, the approach we're taking is that I am like, you might say the creative director and I'm involved with like, 'Okay, here's what we're going to do. Here's some of the ideas.' Then I let the team work on that. And then meanwhile, I'm working on Haunted Chocolatier. "At some point in 1.7's cycle, I will get heavily involved, because I feel like my hand needs to touch every part of the game, every aspect of the update. I need to go over it and adjust it or at least approve everything. So it will require a lot of my time anyway, but I think the balance has been a little bit more shifted, so that I can spend more time focused on Haunted Chocolatier. And I think it's been working out pretty good. That's been a big change from the 1.3 update or 1.1 or something where it's completely me. I had no time to work on a new game. So that has changed. "It is difficult because it's hard to shift gears, I guess. If I'm thinking about Haunted Chocolatier, it's difficult to be like, 'Okay, I'm going to one day of the week or two days of the week work on Stardew Valley.' That's not how my brain works. I'm all in one thing or the other. So I've been trying to work on that. I feel like it requires a lot of discipline, which I'm always working to improve on." We interviewed ConcernedApe and chatted about topics such as the addition of two new marriage candidates with 1.7 , the one secret players still haven't found yet , and why there isn't a Stardew Valley TV show yet . We also chatted with the Stardew Valley community about what the game has meant to them over the years. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: Haunted Chocolatier Is For “The People In Stardew Valley That Go Into The Mines”

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Stardew Valley creator's new game, Haunted Chocolatier, is "more of an action RPG" than farming sim
sources.text: "It's for the people that go into the mines." Stardew Valley creator Eric Barone, has given a new interview - and finally revealed a little more information about his upcoming title, Haunted Chocolatier. In a wide-ranging interview with GQ , which tackles topics ranging from creative burnout to the importance of 'cosy gaming', Barone also slips in some new information about what we can expect from his highly-anticipated Stardew Valley follow-up. And it's all rather surprising. Per the interview, this game is a much more action-oriented affair than the cosy homesteading of Stardew Valley: "It is still what I call a town game," he told GQ, "but it's more of an action RPG - the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights." For anyone that's played Stardew Valley, this won't be a massive shock; there is a combat element to the game, though mostly it's sequestered to one portion of the map - the mines that hold some of the game's rarest materials. If you had fun venturing in there at night to fight slimes and horde minerals, you're going to like Haunted Chocolatier, it seems. "[The new game] is for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly," said Barone. Elsewhere, Barone noted that Haunted Chocolatier is a more "metaphysical" experience than Stardew Valley - which makes sense, I suppose, given its connection to the world of ghosts and spirits - and that "no one's playing the game until I'm ready to show it". Hence, there's still no word on a solid release date. The last update we had on the game was all the way back in January, where Barone noted "I'm alive, the game is still in development" , following up previous statements he made alluding to the fact that the world of Haunted Chocolatier is bigger than Stardew Valley. As for when it's coming out? "The bottom line is, I don’t want to give a release date," Barone said at the start of the year. "The game will come out when it's done." If you want to learn more about the man behind one of video gaming's biggest phenomena of the past few generations, I'd urge you to read the full GQ piece: it's a sensitive, comprehensive look at a man that boasts many talents, yet is also humble and grounded. If you're interested in the musical side of his development process, I profiled Barone once in my column at The Guardian.

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Haunted Chocolatier is for the Stardew Valley players who yearn for the mines, ConcernedApe says
sources.text: Compared to Stardew Valley, ConcernedApe's next game is "more of an action RPG" Good news if you yearn for the mines in Stardew Valley – creator Eric "ConcernedApe" Barone says his long-awaited follow-up game Haunted Chocolatier is for you. In a new interview with GQ , Barone doubles down on an explanation he previously gave of Haunted Chocolatier – even though "it is still what I call a town game," we can expect this one to be "more of an action RPG." He's previously spoken about it having "a greater focus on combat," and he now elaborates: "The main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights." It's the Stardew Valley comparison he makes that really speaks to me, though, and it sounds like Barone and myself have had a very similar experience with his first game. "It's for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines," he says. "That's what I do, honestly." There's still absolutely no word on when we can expect Haunted Chocolatier to launch. Back in August, he apologized that the game is taking so long , but said: "I won't compromise on the quality of the game by rushing it or releasing it too early. Then all my time would be wasted, anyway." This is a sentiment he's doubled down on now, too, saying: "No one's playing the game until I'm ready to show it. If you have a turkey in the oven. You're not going to pull it out halfway and have the guests taste it, right? It needs to be done." So, no Haunted Chocolatier food poisoning for us. Haunted Chocolatier is "way bigger than Stardew Valley," says ConcernedApe: "Everything is cranked up." stories.summary: The No Man's Sky universe is about to get a little bit smaller - but in a good way. Hello Games announced that its long-running sci-fi exploration game will be coming to iOS, with versions for both the iPhone and iPad available starting on October 28th. According to Hello's Sean Murray, the mobile version of […]

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: No Man’s Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
sources.text: A decade later, and the No Man’s Sky updates just keep coming. A decade later, and the No Man’s Sky updates just keep coming. The No Man’s Sky universe is about to get a little bit smaller — but in a good way. Hello Games announced that its long-running sci-fi exploration game will be coming to iOS, with versions for both the iPhone and iPad available starting on October 28th. According to Hello’s Sean Murray, the mobile version of the game is essentially the full No Man’s Sky experience. “I guess I should say this is not No Man’s Sky Lite,” he wrote in a blog post. It includes all of the game’s many, many updates that have come out since launch — like the gigantic Voyagers expansion from last year — and the only major features missing will be multiplayer and the planetary settlements. Murray likens the iOS version to when the game initially launched on the original Switch . “On Switch we have listened to players and built from there, including with a much expanded version on Switch 2 ,” he says. “Based on feedback and player numbers we will support iOS in a similar way.” The game will be playable on the iPhone 11 and 3rd generation iPad Air and above, and the studio says that the download comes in at a surprisingly scant 5GB. It also has newly-designed touch controls, as well as support for controllers, screen casting, and mouse-and-keyboard on the iPad. Murray also notes that “Perhaps most importantly we’ve put tons of work into battery life and thermodynamics, and we’re super proud that No Man’s Sky can be enjoyed for really long comfortable play sessions.” It’ll be “free to try” at launch, though it’s not clear how much the full version will cost. It’s now been a decade since No Man’s Sky first launched, and the game has changed dramatically since its debut. iOS will be joining a huge list of supported platforms, including Mac, PC, and essentially every modern console, and there’s also a VR version available . Just as significant, Hello has continued to keep the game vibrant with a constant stream of free expansions, including the recent Cosmos update in September , which fleshed out the vast expanse of space with more things to explore.

sources.name: Gematsu
sources.title: No Man’s Sky coming to iOS on October 28
sources.text: Hello Games will release No Man’s Sky for iOS on October 28, the company announced. No Man’s Sky is currently available for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store . Here is an overview of the iOS version, via App Store : One-time purchase unlocks the full game which includes 10 years of updates. Inspired by the adventure and imagination that we love from classic science-fiction, No Man’s Sky presents you with a galaxy to explore, filled with unique planets and lifeforms, and constant danger and action. In No Man’s Sky , every star is the light of a distant sun, each orbited by planets filled with life, and you can go to any of them you choose. Fly smoothly from deep space to planetary surfaces, with no loading screens, and no limits. In this infinite procedurally generated universe, you’ll discover places and creatures that no other players have seen before—and perhaps never will again. Play with all major updates since launch: “Foundation,” “Pathfinder,” “Atlas Rises,” “NEXT,” “The Abyss,” “Visions,” the 2.0 “BEYOND” update, “Synthesis,” “Living Ship,” “Exo Mech,” “Desolation” and the 3.0 update, “ORIGINS,” “Next Generation,” “Companions,” “Expeditions,” “Prisms,” “Frontiers,” “Sentinel,” “Outlaws,” “Endurance,” “Waypoint” (4.0), “Fractal,” “Interceptor,” “Echoes,” “Omega,” “Orbital,” “Worlds Part I” (5.0), “Worlds Part II,” “Relics,” “Beacon,” “Voyagers” (6.0), “Remnant,” “Xeno Arena,” “The Swarm,” and “COSMOS” (7.0). An epic voyage to the centre of a shared universe awaits, allowing you to explore, trade, fight and survive. At the centre of the galaxy lies a irresistible pulse which draws you on a journey towards it to learn the true nature of the cosmos. But, facing hostile creatures and fierce pirates, you’ll know that death comes at a cost, and survival will be down to the choices you make over how you upgrade your ship, your weapon and suit. Your voyage through No Man’s Sky is up to you. Will you be a fighter, preying on the weak and taking their riches, or taking out pirates for their bounties? Power is yours if you upgrade your ship for speed and weaponry. Or a trader? Find rich resources on forgotten worlds and exploit them for the highest prices. Invest in more cargo space and you’ll reap huge rewards. Or perhaps an explorer? Go beyond the known frontier and discover places and things that no one has ever seen before. Upgrade your engines to jump ever farther, and strengthen your suit for survival in toxic environments that would kill the unwary. The galaxy is a living, breathing place. Trade convoys travel between stars, factions vie for territory, pirates hunt the unwary, and the police are ever watching. Every other player lives in the same galaxy, and you can choose to share your discoveries with them on a map that spans known space. Perhaps you will see the results of their actions as well as your own…

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: No Man's Sky is somehow coming to mobile, and Hello Games says it's partly thanks to Light No Fire
sources.text: Developer Hello Games has somehow managed to fit its universe-sized space sim No Man's Sky onto iPhone and iPad devices, and it's partly thanks to the studio's upcoming Light No Fire. A decade after its hugely divisive launch and subsequent years-long comeback, No Man's Sky will come to IOS on the 28th of October with all of its numerous updates included. Hello Games promise the game will run on devices going as far back as the iPhone 11, and pre-orders open today. "For nearly three years, we've had this little side project. There's something incredible about this universe fitting in your pocket," studio co-founder Sean Murray said in a deep dive video (below). "We want console quality visuals and gameplay that you can play anywhere. We support touch, we support controllers, even mouse and keyboard. This is something I've loved working on." Murray also explained that Hello Games has made "tons of tweaks and improvements" that should benefit players on all platforms - PC, PlayStation, Switch and Xbox included. But once upon a time, the team thought a mobile port "would never be possible." Of course, iPhones have become increasingly powerful in the decade since No Man's Sky first landed, though there's another reason why the port can even exist and run today: Light No Fire. "We have had to think really hard about where are we going to get this performance from, and how are we going to fit in our memory profile better," Murray said while speaking to Polygon . "And some of those changes have come from Light No Fire. Things that we've been doing there where we've had to make things more performant, we're going, 'Oh, we can carry that across to all of this.' It's all one shared engine." Light No Fire's been away from the spotlight ever since its reveal in 2023 . In case you need reminding, it's a co-op adventure game set on a procedurally generated fantasy planet. While No Man's Sky aims for the stars, the studio's follow-up strips things back ever so slightly to focus on depicting one open-world planet (rather than millions) "with no boundaries" this time. Last month, Murray suggested that Light No Fire was quite far along , but he told Eurogamer (that's us!) that he's learned a "very important lesson of not talking about things" too soon. Alright, then, keep your secrets.

stories.title: Developer Goes Into Debt Spending $1,000 A Day To Keep Steam Demo For AI-Fueled Driving Sim Going
stories.summary: Hoping to launch next year, Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is prematurely sending its creators into the red over exhaustive token use

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Developer Goes Into Debt Spending $1,000 A Day To Keep Steam Demo For AI-Fueled Driving Sim Going
sources.text: Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is an upcoming DMV simulator where players, riding passenger, instruct a chaotic young student to pass their exam. Developers Easy Fox are embracing AI for the project, the titular sister a live chat bot that the player is instructing. Beyond contention for the tech, Easy Fox are finding that the mere demo for the game is proving to be problematic, as accounting for the token usage is forcing them into debt . “Over the past month, the number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold,” reads the Steam pageâs latest update . “Thank you so much for giving our game far more attention than we ever expected. This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably.” As the update explains, the game originally patched players through to a chat bot operating on Googleâs Gemini. With no cost barrier between them and the curious, players of the demo were triggering limit-use errors, Google informing Easy Fox that thereâs no easy way out. Switching to the competing OpenAI model, while hoping to finding a fix with Gemini, is proving to be the least of their problems. Easy Fox says the surge of players has forced them to take out a bank loan to keep the demo operating. Maintaining the demo is apparently costing them more than $1,000 a day, which they admit they will have to factor into pricing the final product. While a number of game developers have flocked to AI to create in-game assets and code on the back-end, Teach My Little Sister is a more unique case. Leveraging an agent for sustained real-time gameplay, the game has found an expensive way to recreate what Lifeline and Hey You, Pikachu! accomplished over 20 years ago. “We want to continue operating the demo and would love for more people to enjoy it,” writes Easy Fox. “However, we are a small team of four, and financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release. We have not made that decision at this time.” The update also addresses complaints that, even in a game based around calamity, the AI fueled sister is not following instructions as desired. While a microcosm of it, the financial strain is an amusing illustration of one of AIâs biggest white elephant. That is, no oneâs sure how to make money off of it. While proliferating in short video content, horrifying fast food posters and visual assets devs “meant to take out,” the firms themselves are running purely on investments, not generating profit. The amount of resources needed to keep these computers burning continually outweighs what the public is otherwise willing to spend to see SpongeBob murder Shrek . Over the last year, AI firms have been forced to adjust, adding new premiums to their service, the so-called “tokenpocalypse.” With the global economy now held hostage by the industry, the burdens of the tech continue to put people on edge. Easy Fox are being taught a swift lesson on something the global population is likely going to learn the hard way. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. The director has released his own Claude-driven adventure having spent months praising the technology It also broke the record for the number of players in-game by another half a million As Affleck seeks to establish a seat for movie stars at AI's table, his use-case political thriller Animals isn't exactly persuasive Call of Duty: Black Ops , Halo: CE , Grand Theft Auto: Vice City , Skate 3 and many more titles have been decompiled and ported to web browsers overnight Get ready for the vision that is Space Corridor Astrocade is filled with AI slop, but millions of people don't seem to care

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: The developer of an AI-powered driving instruction simulator is spending $1,000 per month just to keep its demo running
sources.text: Teach My Little Sister How to Drive centres around a costly chatbot. One of the many ways AI will (supposedly) revolutionise the games industry is facilitating highly reactive NPCs via LLM-powered chatbots. Yet so far, only a handful of games like Where Winds Meet have attempted to implement the tech, and the results have been less than spectacular. But there might also be another reason why relatively few games feature LLM-powered NPCs, which is that powering such chatbots can be costly, as recently demonstrated by the developers of an upcoming driving instructor simulator As reported by FRVR (via Kotaku ) Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is a comic simulation game in which you coach your virtual sibling on driving technique from the comfort of the passenger seat. The twist is that behind your sister's dinner-plate eyes is an LLM chatbot (currently powered by an OpenAI model, though the developers intend to use Gemini for the final release) In the role of instructor, players can both converse with the chatbot and issue vocal instructions such as "turn left here", to which the bot will respond accordingly. At least, that's the theory. Developer Easy Fox released a demo for Teach My Little Sister How To Drive back in February, but in the past month the game has seen a surge in players, which has had an interesting knock-on effect for the demo. "The number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold," Easy Fox explained in a Steam post , adding. "This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably." Easy Fox goes on to explain that it is "spending over $1,000 per day on AI services for the demo", as players burn through tokens prompting the LLM by proxy. Easy Fox claims that figure "isn't because each player is particularly expensive to support", but rather that "so many people are playing." As a result of this, Easy Fox has "taken out a bank loan to help keep the demo running". Yet even this may not be sufficient to support the demo long term. "Financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release," Easy Fox says, though the studio stresses it has "not made that decision at this time". According to FRVR, that twentyfold increase in players amounts to 450 concurrent. While the overall player numbers will be higher than that, it isn't an enormous figure, and it makes me wonder how financially viable the game will be when it is released. Easy Fox says it will "account for expected AI usage in the game's price". But it also says that players "will not be charged separately for their individual AI token usage after purchasing the game". That might work in the short term, but surely those token costs are going to pile up over time. It's also worth noting that AI token costs are highly unpredictable , with even large companies like Microsoft and Uber struggling to accurately predict the cost and burn rate of their own internal token use. In its Steam post, Easy Fox says it's looking into options like introducing local AI models for players with "sufficiently capable GPUs". But that's only going to be a fraction of the player-base. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. All of this is aside from whether an AI-powered driving instruction game is a good idea. Personally, I think the fact that it revolves specifically around chatting with another character makes this a more sensible application than in Where Winds Meet, where the chatbots don't factor into the game design in any meaningful way. It's much more reminiscent of early chatbot-based social sim Façade . But the very fact it reminds me of Façade makes me wonder whether the game needs a premium LLM connected to it to achieve its goal. Easy Fox states that current design problems being addressed include "dialogue that feels too artificial and breaks immersion" and "commands being carried out incorrectly, such as turning right when asked to turn left." All of which seems like it could be solved with a good voice actor and a sufficiently rich dialogue system. Easy Fox plans to release the full game in January next year, so we'll find out exactly how the finances stack up then. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. While he'll play anything that can be controlled with a keyboard and mouse, he has a particular passion for first-person shooters and immersive sims. stories.title: Entenda os 5 diferentes finais de Silent Hill: Townfall
stories.summary: O final de Townfall é determinado por algumas ações ao longo do jogo

sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Entenda os 5 diferentes finais de Silent Hill: Townfall
sources.text: Silent Hill: Townfall , o novo spin-off desenvolvido pela Screen Burnem parceria com a Konami, chega para expandir o universo da franquia em um cenário inédito . Desta vez, estamos na isolada ilha escocesa de St. Amelia, em 1996. O protagonista, Simon Ordell, é convocado de volta à cidade para “colocar as coisas em ordem”, mas encontra apenas uma névoa densa cobrindo ruas aparentemente abandonadas. Apesar de não se passar na cidade famosa da franquia, o tipo de contexto é basicamente o mesmo. Seguindo a tradição de jogos da série, Townfall não conta com um final único. Em vez disso, as ações do jogador ao longo da campanha determinam qual desfecho a história vai tomar. Para te ajudar a entender melhor o conceito, listamos os todos os finais de Silent Hill: Townfall e te contamos o que é necessário para conseguir cada um deles. Confira! Como revelado previamente pelos desenvolvedores, o jogo conta com 5 finais diferentes, sendo que 2 são secretos. Assim como em jogos anteriores da série, as decisões tomadas pelo jogador ao longo da aventura é que definem o desfecho, até para que o final pareça coerente com a experiência vivida durante a partida. Não existe uma escolha explícita em algum momento marcante do enredo que define isso, já que o final é determinado por alguns elementos diferentes. O sistema acompanha o comportamento do jogador durante toda a partida, incluindo o quanto ele explora e investiga St. Amelia e o quão agressivo ele é ao ser confrontado por inimigos, em contraste com evitar ou fugir dos combates. Essa abordagem lembra diretamente o clássico Silent Hill 2 , em que o final também refletia padrões de comportamento e não escolhas de diálogo, por exemplo. Dos 5 desfechos possíveis , 3 estão disponíveis já na primeira vez que você zera a campanha , sem necessidade de repetir o jogo. Já os outros 2 finais secretos exigem uma segunda campanha jogada no modo New Game Plus. Esses 3 finais “normais” são chamados de Justice, Forever e Abandoned e são considerados os desfechos principais da trama de Simon. Eles são determinados exclusivamente pela relação entre quantos inimigos o jogador elimina durante a partida e quantas descobertas, como pistas e documentos, ele coleta ao longo do caminho. O tempo de jogo ou uso de itens de cura não influencia nesse resultado. Também é bom mencionar que que esse equilíbrio entre mortes e descobertas afeta apenas a cena final antes dos créditos, sem alterar outras cenas ou a progressão da história ao longo da campanha. Até por isso, você é que tem lembrar de como quer abordar o jogo para conseguir o final desejado. Conforme mencionamos, além dos 3 finais principais, o jogo reserva 2 desfechos extras classificados como secretos , chamados de Dog e Sci-fi. Quem é fã veterano da franquia Silent Hill sabe que esses são finais absolutamente clássicos e colocados no jogo apenas como uma brincadeira extra para o jogador se divertir. Por serem uma piada, é necessário zerar o game uma vez para conseguir um final sério e, então, zerá-lo uma segunda vez no New Game Plus para ter acesso aos desfechos secretos. Como explicado acima, o sistema de finais de Townfall não depende de escolhas de diálogo ou momentos de decisão específicos, mas sim do comportamentos do jogador ao longo de toda a campanha. Para facilitar, nós listamos o que é necessário para cada um. O final Justice é considerado por muitos como o desfecho “bom” da história. Ele é obtido ao final de uma campanha em que o número de descobertas, na forma de pistas e documentos coletados, é significativamente maior do que o número de inimigos eliminados. A boa notícia é que é possível ter dezenas de eliminações e ainda assim alcançar esse final, até porque alguns confrontos ao longo da aventura são praticamente inevitáveis. Por isso, só tente ter certeza de que a quantidade de descobertas seja bem superior. O final Forever é tratado como o desfecho “normal” do jogo. Ele surge quando a quantidade de descobertas é apenas ligeiramente maior do que a quantidade de eliminações ao término da campanha. Diferente do Justice, aqui a margem entre pistas coletadas e inimigos mortos é bem mais estreita, exigindo um equilíbrio mais cuidadoso por parte do jogador ao longo da aventura. Já o Abandoned é considerado o final “ruim” da história. Ele ocorre sempre que o número de inimigos eliminados supera o número de descobertas feitas até o fim do jogo. Para quem opta por um estilo de jogo mais agressivo, ignorando documentos e pistas em favor do combate direto, esse desfecho é praticamente garantido. O final “Dog” é um dos desfechos secretos, exclusivos do New Game Plus. Ele é desbloqueado ao encontrar três moedas especiais espalhadas por diferentes áreas da cidade durante a nova campanha. Com as moedas em mãos, você precisa depositá-las em cofres em formato de cachorro, ligados a uma instituição de cães-guia presente no cenário do jogo. Completar essa sequência de itens substitui o final principal que o jogador obteria normalmente. O Sci-fi é o segundo final secreto, também restrito ao New Game Plus. Para obtê-lo, é necessário interagir com três livros específicos escondidos em diferentes pontos da campanha, resolver um quebra-cabeça de porta usando um código, e por fim utilizar um item especial obtido nesse processo em um painel eletrônico próximo ao fim da aventura. Diferente dos demais finais, o Sci-fi é acionado antes da batalha final, pulando completamente esse confronto e levando direto ao desfecho. Se não quiser spoilers sobre os finais de Silent Hill: Townfall, é melhor pular essa parte do nosso guia! No final “Justice”, Simon consegue encarar os traumas do seu passado de frente, encontrando uma resolução pacífica e libertadora para a sua culpa. No final “Forever”, o protagonista se recusa a aceitar os fatos totalmente e decide permanecer preso na névoa e nas memórias da ilha. No final Abandoned, dominado pela raiva e violência, Simon sucumbe totalmente ao pesadelo e se torna parte do ciclo de sofrimento do loc

sources.title: GTA 6 Leaker Posts Grainy Footage Of Lucia Skydiving Naked To Sell Crypto
sources.text: Cyberleek Grand Theft Auto 6 Grand Theft Auto VI GTA 6 Leaks Lucia Rockstar Games After going quiet for over a month following the Grand Theft Auto 6 extended reveal on Netflix , the account Cyberleek has been busy over the last few days with fresh gameplay leaks and threats. The unknown user claimed they would release a playable build of the game if their crypto meme coin hit a $30 million market cap, and they’re now posting footage of Lucia naked to try to drive up the price. The latest leak shows the game’s female lead driving around the city, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and visiting an ATM. It also spends a significant amount of time with the Parachuting side mission and mini-games teased in the previous gameplay reveal . The footage also looks janky in parts, leaving viewers to wonder just how old the build it’s from is.market cap The latest Lucia footage comes as the leaker polls people online for what should be released next. They’re promising to release longer and more detailed versions of “ naked Lucia ” the more people buy into their crypto scheme. Cyberleek reveals that he has access to Lucia fully naked in GTA 6, and will publish the footage depending on his tokenâs marketcap. Heâs using this tactic to manipulate people into his pump-and-dump crypto scheme again, so beware. pic.twitter.com/6q0PmoVOIA — GTA 6 Countdown â³ (@GTAVI_Countdown) October 10, 2026 The existing theory is that Cyberleek is using some sort of older build or debug mode to show off the game’s two protagonists without any clothes on, and that it’s unclear if this is a thing that can happen in the actual story campaign itself. Bystanders in the world don’t react to Lucia being naked in the latest leak, suggesting something else is indeed going on . Whatever the account has access to, it’s threatening to release it if enough people buy its $Cyberleek meme coin. It’s currently at a market cap of around $4.75 million , up significantly since the leaker’s apparent return. But that’s still a very long way from $30 million. The account has also claimed that Take-Two can avoid a threatened release of some version of GTA 6 if it releases a disc version of the game and “apologizes” to players. Any semblance of some pro-consumer stance has been undercut by the preparation for another attempt at a crypto rug pull. The last time Cyberleek went quiet, the account seemingly made off with roughly $250,000 in dumped crypto . With just over a month until GTA 6’s release, it’s not gunning for a much bigger payday. sources.title: 'GTA 6' Leaker's Naked Lucia Gamble Just Backfired Massively
sources.text: 'Cyberleek' made a huge tactical error in sharing GTA 6 gameplay of Lucia Caminos nude For a while, it seemed like Take-Two and Rockstar Games were facing a doomsday scenario that could have seen a playable build of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaked to the public a month before its official release. Cyberleek, the leaker behind the scheme, was encouraging people to invest at least $30 million into a meme cryptocurrency in order to earn GTA 6 's apparent development build. To reach that number, the leaker tied early investment milestones to footage of GTA 6 co-protagonist, Lucia Caminos, fully nude. Well, viewers readily donated to see the character's digital privates — but now, fans who have had their fill are pulling their money back out. The early market cap milestones were all tied to Lucia in some way: a couple of millions of dollars to see her in a bikini; a few million to get gameplay showing Lucia topless. To get Lucia fully naked, GTA 6 fans had to raise $4 million in Cyberleek's cryptocurrency. For $6 million, Cyberleek promised fans would receive naked Lucia gameplay clips in 4K resolution. All of these milestones were smashed within hours, resulting in a frenzy among horny gamers on social media. GTA 6 fans were sharing GIFs and videos of Lucia skydiving naked or were posting crass comments about the character's body in thousands of social media posts. Fans had been begging Cyberleek for such footage since the start of the leaks back in August, so the unauthorized gameplay was a big deal for gooners. Less than 24 hours after reaching such highs, Cyberleek's ploy has officially crashed. Prior to the chaos, the Cyberleek coin only had a market cap of just under $1.7 million. At the peak of trading, the market cap reached a high of $8.2 million. Cyberleek dumped their developer tokens earlier this year, so the leaker couldn't have been the engine behind the 71% drop. The leaker could still have enjoyed a big payday from the overarching ruckus thanks to transaction fees, but the bulk of the money coming out of the market cap appears to be outside investors. Despite this mass exodus, Cyberleek is still trying to tempt GTA 6 fans with new milestones. These rewards include gameplay clips of things like tank sequences, a private lap dance, and a beach massacre. Cyberleek posted one set of milestones and updated them with a wider assortment of tiers within only a couple of hours. The end prize remained the same: at $30 million, GTA 6 fans would supposedly receive a development build of the game. Based on the current crash, GTA 6 fans aren't biting. "He's already over played his hand with the lucia gooners leak," one Redditor remarked . Cyberleek correctly surmised that footage of Lucia naked could entice desperate gamers, but the leaker made the tactical error of offering their most valuable asset at the lowest possible tiers. Between now and release, Rockstar itself could show new details like tank or jet gameplay, and the Netflix Extended Look has already shown people what a GTA 6 police shootout scene looks like. The only aspects of GTA 6 that could feasibly remain under wraps until after release were the sexual bits, like the nude encampment. And even that much wouldn't entirely be new: Rockstar has already published screenshots of GTA 6 lap dances. "The only people that would have invested in his stupid fucking coin would have been horny high schoolers that dont know how to manage money," another Redditor wrote. "Now he fucked that all up." Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

especial_gta6.tema: Lucia Caminos: quem é a protagonista de GTA 6
especial_gta6.angulo: Quem é Lucia, a lutadora recém-saída da cadeia que divide o protagonismo de GTA 6 com Jason, e o que o jogo já mostrou dela antes do lançamento.

fatos.texto: Lucia Caminos é uma das duas protagonistas de GTA 6, ao lado de Jason Duval.
Segundo o perfil oficial, o pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar assim que ela aprendeu a andar.
Lutar pela própria família a levou para a Penitenciária de Leonida.
Ela saiu da prisão por pura sorte, e agora quer fazer só jogadas inteligentes.
Lucia quer a vida boa que a mãe sonha desde a época em que as duas viviam em Liberty City, e está disposta a resolver as coisas com as próprias mãos.
Para a Rockstar, uma vida ao lado de Jason pode ser a saída de Lucia.
Falas de Lucia no site oficial incluem "A única coisa que importa é quem você conhece e o que você tem".
Os trailers mostram Lucia deixando a prisão; no Trailer 2, é Jason quem vai buscá-la.

Na sinopse oficial, Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas estavam marcadas contra eles; quando um golpe fácil dá errado, os dois caem no lado mais sombrio de Vice City, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que se espalha pelo estado de Leonida, e precisam confiar um no outro para sair vivos.
A Rockstar publicou os perfis oficiais dos personagens no site de GTA VI em 6 de maio de 2025, no mesmo dia em que lançou o Trailer 2.

O vídeo 'Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look', com cerca de 26 minutos de jogo capturado no PS5, estreou na Netflix em 27 de agosto de 2026 às 15h (horário de Nova York, 16h em Brasília) e chegou ao YouTube da Rockstar às 21h (22h em Brasília) do mesmo dia.
No Extended Look, Lucia pergunta a Jason qual roupa usar antes de uma festa na casa de Brian Heder.
O vídeo mostra Lucia treinando: ela aparece fazendo sparring e supino.
Em combates corpo a corpo, Lucia pode atacar usando um salto alto, segundo cenas mostradas pela Rockstar.
No trecho final, Jason e Lucia fazem a segurança de um evento corporativo que é atacado; no fim do vídeo, Lucia está em perigo.
Rumor, sem confirmação da Rockstar: a atriz Manni L. Perez é apontada como a intérprete de Lucia; a Dexerto afirma que 'a Rockstar ainda não confirmou' e a SVG lembra que o elenco não foi anunciado.
Perez já teve um papel pequeno em GTA V: segundo a Dexerto, ela aparece nos créditos como duas crupiês de blackjack sem nome no cassino Diamond.

GTA 6 sai em 19 de novembro de 2026 para PS5 e Xbox Series X|S, segundo o site oficial e a GameSpot (agosto de 2026); em maio de 2025 a Rockstar havia anunciado 26 de maio de 2026, data que depois foi adiada.
